source: Execution-runs API latest activity attempts and original real request plan assignments
finding: Private uploads are approximately four seconds; whole-workspace receiver verification/merge and the variable post-transfer launch interval remain substantially larger than estimated edge transfer time. The 196-second launch interval is not network upload time.
nextMeasurement: Separate remote directory preparation, full workspace snapshot, Docker launch (which can include image pull), and initial telemetry. Instrumentation is committed locally but not deployed into the healthy running daemon.
limitations: API runtime is an observed task interval; these entries do not independently prove pure application compute duration.
Transfer work sums overlapping dependency records and must not be interpreted as elapsed preparation time.
Reported queue time includes waits before launch and is not evidence of Slurm queue duration for these cloud tasks.
Recovered execution, potentially warm workspaces/images, approximate micro speedup and uncalibrated prices preclude claiming an uninterrupted calibrated benchmark.
Estimated plan edge volume and real whole-workspace bytes are different contracts. No scope or integrity reduction was made.
